Summer Universiade|2015 Gwangju]] | [[United States men's national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Wayne Anthony Selden Jr.''' (born September 30, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Chorale Roanne Basket|Chorale Roanne]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. ==High school career== Selden first attended [[John D. O'Bryant School of Mathematics & Science|John D. O'Bryant]] as a [[freshman (education)|freshman]] before transferring to [[Tilton School]], where he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the class of 2014 and repeated the [[ninth grade]].{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Five-star prospect Wayne Selden reclassifies back to 2013|date=June 8, 2012|work=CBS Sports|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/five-star-prospect-wayne-selden-reclassifies-back-to-2013/|access-date=March 11, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Now in 2013, Wayne Selden turns eye toward recruitment|date=July 3, 2012|work=CBS Sports|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/now-in-2013-wayne-selden-turns-eye-toward-recruitment/|access-date=March 11, 2023}} In 2012, he reclassified back to the class of 2013. He averaged 24.8 points, 10.1 rebounds and four assists during his [[senior (education)|senior]] year, earning McDonald's All-American. He was the East team's second-leading scorer in the McDonald's All-American game, going 5-for-7 from the field, 2-for-4 from three-point range, for 13 points with five rebounds and three assists and played in the Jordan Brand Classic game. When he graduated, he was considered a five-star player and was ranked No. 14 on the ESPN 100 and No. 12 by Rivals.com.{{cite web|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5201|title=Player Profile: #1 Wayne Selden Jr.|date=July 9, 2013 |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks|access-date=April 6, 2014}} ==College career== Selden played three years of college basketball for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. As a junior in [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2015–16]], he earned second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] honors and was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]].{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}} He appeared in 38 games (37 starts) for the Jayhawks during his junior season and averaged 13.8 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 29.9 minutes while shooting 47.4 percent from the field, 39.2 percent from three-point range and 61.2 percent from the free throw line. On March 29, 2016, Selden declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/news/2016/3/29/mens-basketball-selden-declares-for-nba-draft-leaves-ku.aspx|title=Selden Declares for NBA Draft, Leaves KU|work=kuathletics.com|date=March 29, 2016|access-date=August 8, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Iowa Energy (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Selden signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on August 8, 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/selden-stephens-williams-wroten-signed-160808|title=Grizzlies sign Wayne Selden Jr., D.J. Stephens, Troy Williams and Tony Wroten|work=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2016|access-date=August 8, 2016}} He was waived by the Grizzlies on October 22, 2016, after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/sampson-selden-stephens-waived-161022|title=Grizzlies waive JaKarr Sampson, Wayne Selden Jr. & D.J. Stephens|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}} Seven days later, he was acquired by the [[Iowa Wolves|Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate of the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://iowa.dleague.nba.com/news/energy-announce-returning-affiliate-tryout-players-2/|title=Energy Announce Returning, Affiliate and Tryout Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016|archive-date=February 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216050317/http://iowa.dleague.nba.com/news/energy-announce-returning-affiliate-tryout-players-2/|url-status=dead}} In 35 games for Iowa, he averaged 18.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 30.6 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-wayne-selden-jr-10-day-contract|title=Pelicans Sign Wayne Selden Jr. to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=March 8, 2017}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2017)=== On March 8, 2017, Selden signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He made his NBA debut six days later,{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pelicans-wayne-selden-will-start-at-shooting-guard-tuesday/|title=Pelicans' Wayne Selden: Will start at shooting guard Tuesday|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 14, 2017|access-date=March 14, 2017}} recording two points, three rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes as a starter in a 100–77 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400900397|title=Trail Blazers vs. Pelicans – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=March 14, 2017|access-date=March 14, 2017}} On March 17, 2017, in his third career NBA game, Selden scored 11 points in a 128–112 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900419|title=Hill's career-high 30 lead Pelicans past Rockets 128-112|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2017–2019)=== On March 18, 2017, following the expiration of his 10-day contract with New Orleans, Selden signed a multi-year contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/wayne-selden-signed-douglas-waived-170318|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Wayne Selden Jr.|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} On April 7, 2017, he scored a career-high 13 points in a 101–88 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900559|title=Conley scores 31, Grizzlies beat Knicks to clinch seventh|work=ESPN.com|date=April 7, 2017|access-date=April 8, 2017}} In his playoff debut on April 15, 2017, he recorded five points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal while starting in Game 1 of the Grizzlies' first-round match-up with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/seldewa01/gamelog/2017/|title=Wayne Selden 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 1, 2017}} On July 1, 2017, Selden signed a new multi-year contract with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/selden-signed-to-multi-year-contract-160701|title=Grizzlies sign Wayne Selden Jr. to a multi-year contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2017|access-date=July 1, 2017}} On November 10, 2017, he was assigned to the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite Hustle|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2017|access-date=January 2, 2018}} He played that night and was recalled by the Grizzlies the following day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-recall-davis-selden-17111|title=Grizzlies recall Deyonta Davis and Wayne Selden Jr. from Memphis Hustle|work=ESPN.com|date=November 11, 2017|access-date=January 2, 2018}} Selden missed much of the first half of the 2017–18 season with a right quad injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975299|title=Williams leads Clippers past Grizzlies, 113-105|work=ESPN.com|date=January 2, 2018|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On January 20, 2018, he scored a career-high 31 points in a 111–104 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975423|title=Holiday, Cousins, Davis lead Pelicans past Memphis 111-104|work=ESPN.com|date=January 20, 2018|access-date=January 20, 2018}} ===Chicago Bulls (2019)=== On January 3, 2019, Selden was traded, along with [[MarShon Brooks]] and the Grizzlies' 2019 and 2020 second-round picks, to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for
